name: Lateral raise
pattern: Shoulder abduction: straight-ish arms lift out to the sides to about shoulder height and lower again.
setup: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in.
Soft bend in the elbows, about 10-20°.
Arms a little in front of your body, about 30° (the scapular plane).

steps.text: Lift the arms out to the sides, leading with the elbows.
Stop at about shoulder height, hands level with or just below the elbows.
Lower slowly back to your sides.

cues.cue: Thumbs level or slightly up, do not pour the jug.
cues.why: Raising with the arm turned in shifts work to the rear delt and upper trap and is the empty-can position; neutral gives the most side-delt.
Above about 90° the shoulder must rotate out to clear the bony arch; without it the cuff can pinch.
Shrugging lets the upper trap lift the weight instead of the side delt.

cues.cue: Arms slightly forward of your sides.
cues.why: In the scapular plane the shoulder blade and humerus move together with the least strain.

cues.cue: No swing: stand still, slow on the way down.
cues.why: Leaning and swinging turn the lift into momentum and load the lower back.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.

mistakes.name: Shrugging
mistakes.looks: Shoulders rise toward the ears as the arms go up.
mistakes.fix: Lighter weight, push shoulders down, stop at shoulder height.
mistakes.why: The upper trap takes over from the side delt.

mistakes.name: Swinging the body
mistakes.looks: Knees dip and the trunk rocks back to throw the weights up.
mistakes.why: Momentum lifts the weight and the side delt does less.

mistakes.name: Pouring the jug
mistakes.looks: Thumbs turn down and the little finger leads.
mistakes.fix: Keep thumbs level or a bit up.
mistakes.why: The turned-in arm narrows the space under the shoulder bone and shifts work to the rear delt and upper trap.

mistakes.name: Raising too high
mistakes.looks: Hands go well above the head line.
mistakes.why: Raising past about 90° while turned in pinches the cuff.

safety: Shoulder pain: stay below 80°, thumbs up, arms in the scapular plane.
Use light weights; the side delt has a long lever and small loads are enough.

variants.change: Cable from the opposite side: tension stays on at the bottom.
Leaning or lying on your side: more load near the bottom of the arc.
Elbows bent about 90°: shorter lever, easier.
Partial reps: only the top or bottom half.
Lu raise: thumbs up, keep going overhead until the hands meet; light weight.
One arm: hold a post with the other hand for a still trunk.
Chest on an incline bench: no swing.

subtypes.name: Y raise
subtypes.change: Arms lift up and out into a Y, about 30° in front of the body line, thumbs up. Often done face down on an incline bench for the lower traps.

subtypes.name: Side-lying raise
subtypes.change: Lying on your side (floor or bench), lift the top arm from across the body up to vertical; the load is hardest at the start.

subtypes.name: Machine lateral raise
subtypes.change: Seated, pads on the outside of the arms or elbows; same arm path.

motion.basis: Scapular upward rotation scaled from the glenohumeral to scapular ratio of about 1.7:1 in the scapular plane (mcclure2001; about 28° at 90° arm elevation including a resting value of about 5°, estimate). Arm height and plane from schoenfeld2011 and mcclure2001. Shoulder rotation is neutral by design (coratella2020: neutral raise gave the most medial deltoid); with palms in at the start and no rotation the palms face down at the top, so the forearm stays at 0.

sources.cite: Coratella G, Tornatore G, Longo S, Esposito F, Cè E. An electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders. Int J Environ Res Public Health. 2020;17(17):6015.
